How it was made

  • PJ's line-art turnaround
  • rendered to clay, front + back
  • 3D reconstruction
  • this mesh

What came through

  • The head survived. Slab stack, side lobes, the grin — no drift toward a human skull.
  • Feet and hands are present and separated, with toes.

What's still wrong

  • The profile is guessed. Built from front and back only, so from a dead side angle the head reads thin and slightly lopsided. Side views are the next thing to draw.
  • Surface detail is soft. The teeth and carved eyes didn't survive — a resolution cap, not a design problem.
  • Not print-ready. Ankles and fingers fall under the 2 mm minimum, and the mesh isn't watertight.
A blockout for looking at, not a file for printing. Front and 3/4 are the honest angles — the side is the machine filling in a gap. Same file is on GitHub if you want to download it.
